statistics.locator: Results, paragraph on the after-effect phase (pointing without visual feedback)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant factor (Episode), not a between-group comparison of old vs young.
statistics.notes: Effect of the within-factor Episode across the five after-effect episodes.

statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.direction_quote: indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term (Age × Episode), not a between-group main effect on the outcome.
statistics.notes: The paper's qualitative statement is about the rate of decline of the after-effect, not about which group had the larger after-effect magnitude.

statistics.effect_as_written: Age (main effect) in the after-effect ANOVA
statistics.direction_quote: the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups
statistics.admissible_reason: No statistic for the Age main effect on the after-effect is printed on these pages.
statistics.notes: For the after-effect phase the text reports only Episode and the interaction; no F or p for the between-factor Age is given. The prose states 'the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups, and gradually declined with practice; this age-independence is in marked contrast with the findings during adaptation', implying a non-significant Age effect, but no number is printed.

statistics.admissible_reason: No standardised effect size is printed for this outcome.
statistics.notes: These pages report only F values with P thresholds (and one t test for the trail-making test); no d, g, or partial eta-squared appears anywhere.

parsed.notes: The after-effect analysis on page 3 reports only the within-factor Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the Age × Episode interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); no main effect of Age is quantified for this phase, and the text explicitly describes the after-effect as 'similar in both age groups'. Other F values on the page belong to different phases/outcomes (adaptation phase Age F(1,22)=7.58; refresh phase Age F(1,22)=13.42; episodes 20 vs 26 Age F(1,22)=13.78; tracking transfer Procedure F(1,43)=144.09) and the t(22)=5.25 belongs to the trail-making test, so none were transcribed as this outcome. No group means or SDs for the after-effect episodes are given in text; they appear only in Fig. 1.
